newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 21.62 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 21.62 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs fell 256 basis points to 21.62 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.
The Central Bank said it sold 15 billion bolivars of the 179-day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills at a price of 101.15 pct. The bills carried a 24.18 percent coupon.

The bank also sold 10 billion bolivars of 269-day notes with a 24.90 percent coupon at a price of 101.01 percent, and 10 billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 25.64 percent coupon at an average price of 100.28 percent.
According to the Reuters calculation, yields for the other notes fell to 23.31 percent for the 269-day bills, and 25.28 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The yields for 179-, 269-, and 358-day bills sold at last week's auction were 24.18 percent, 26.20 percent and 27.71 percent respectively.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
